articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada neste sábado (3), véspera do 1º turno, mostra como está a disputa pelo governo da Paraíba. Lucas Ribeiro (PP) aparece com 61% dos votos válidos e pode ser reeleito no primeiro turno.

Lucas Ribeiro (PP) à esquerda, Efraim Filho (PL) ao centro e Cícero Lucena (MDB) à direita, candidatos ao governo da Paraíba — Foto: Gustavo Demétrio/g1 PB

É a forma como o TSE divulga o resultado oficial das eleições. São os votos dados nos candidatos. Esse cálculo deixa de fora os votos em branco e nulos e abstenções. Para vencer no 1º turno, um candidato precisa de 50% dos votos válidos mais um voto.

Votos válidos para o governo da Paraíba, de acordo com a pesquisa Quaest — Foto: TV Cabo Branco

A Quaest leva em consideração as intenções de voto da pesquisa e o perfil de comparecimento para estimar os votos válidos. É o modelo likely voter, que considera eleitores com maior propensão a votar.

O levantamento foi encomendado pelas TVs Cabo Branco e Paraíba e ouviu 1.800 eleitores de 16 anos ou mais, entre os dias 2 e 3 de outubro. A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa foi registrada na Justiça Eleitoral sob o número PB-05048/2026.

Veja agora o resultado com os votos totais, incluindo votos em branco, nulos e eleitores indecisos.

Lucas Ribeiro (PP): 52% (eram 49% em 22/09)

A candidatura de Pedro Coutinho se tornou inapta após o registro desta pesquisa.

Veja agora a pesquisa espontânea, em que os eleitores respondem sem ter acesso a uma lista de candidatos.

Esses resultados ajudam a medir o grau de consolidação do voto. Quanto maior o número de indecisos na véspera, menos consolidado está o voto e maior a possibilidade de mudanças em relação ao resultado de domingo.

Entre os eleitores que declaram voto em um candidato, 84% dizem que a decisão é definitiva. Outros 15% afirmam que ainda podem mudar de ideia.

articles.title: Quase 290 mil indígenas estão aptos a votar neste domingo (4) em todo o país | G1
articles.standfirst: Para garantir o direito ao voto, a Justiça Eleitoral leva urnas até aldeias isoladas.
articles.summary: Para garantir o direito ao voto, a Justiça Eleitoral leva urnas até aldeias isoladas.
articles.body:
Quase 290 mil indígenas estão aptos a votar neste domingo (4) em todo o país. Para garantir o direito ao voto, a Justiça Eleitoral leva urnas até aldeias isoladas.

O TRE levou de avião cinco urnas até a aldeia Pavuru, no Parque Indígena do Xingu, em Mato Grosso. Duas para a votação e três de reserva; 554 indígenas de 21 aldeias da região devem votar neste domingo (4). E alguns também serão mesários.

“Envolve uma logística bastante grande e bastante extensa, não só na distância, mas também nos horários”, conta Adriano dos Santos, coordenador da operação.

Para alguns eleitores, o desafio é chegar. O trajeto de barco pelo Rio Xingu pode levar de seis a nove horas. O transporte é garantido pela Justiça Eleitoral, para permitir que moradores de aldeias distantes também possam participar da votação.

“A gente tem que chegar antes aqui para a gente não perder o horário. De repente, na nossa viagem, pode acontecer imprevisto”, diz o indígena Awa Kaiabi.

Quase 290 mil indígenas estão aptos a votar neste domingo (4) em todo o país — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Em Rondônia, o transporte das urnas começou na quinta-feira (1º) para atender mais de 7 mil indígenas e quilombolas. No Amazonas, as urnas começaram a chegar na sexta-feira (2), de barco, em comunidades na região de Parintins. Uma viagem de cinco horas para os mesários, que levam mais do que a urna até as aldeias.

“A confiança, o respeito sobre a democracia. Isso aí vale a pena para todo mundo hoje, para o povo brasileiro”, afirma o mesário Zacarias Ferreira.

“A gente começa a discutir, se organizar para poder cobrar depois. Assim que esse candidato ganhar, e cobrar dele o que nós estamos necessitando aqui na aldeia”, diz o professor Iokore Kawakum Ikpeng.

articles.standfirst: Sorteio deste sábado (3) pode pagar cerca R$ 82 milhões.
articles.summary: Sorteio deste sábado (3) pode pagar cerca R$ 82 milhões.
articles.body:
O sorteio do concurso 3066 da Mega-Sena foi realizado, excepcionalmente, na noite deste sábado (3), em São Paulo. A mudança aconteceu por conta das eleições que serão realizadas neste domingo (4). Quem acertar as seis dezenas pode receber cerca de R$ 82 milhões.

Veja os números sorteados: 04 - 06 - 09 - 13 - 28 - 48

A Caixa ainda não divulgou se houve ganhadores para o sorteio.

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet, até as 20h – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

A Mega tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, quintas e domingos .

A aposta mínima custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet, até as 20h – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Os jogos podem ser realizados até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.body:
Cartão Pra Já no BRT Metropolitano. — Foto: Divulgação

Os eleitores que precisam se deslocar entre os municípios da região metropolitana de Belém no dia da votação terão BRT Metropolitano operando com catraca livre neste domingo (4), data em que ocorre o primeiro turno das eleições municipais.

Segundo o governo, a medida é para garantir o direito ao voto e facilitar o acesso dos cidadãos aos respectivos colégios eleitorais sem custos com transporte público.

O sistema de integração do BRT Metropolitano conecta a capital paraense a outras seis cidades da região. Com a gratuidade garantida, os passageiros poderão transitar sem o pagamento de tarifa entre os seguintes municípios:

Para dar conta do fluxo de eleitores, a Agência de Regulação e Controle de Serviços Públicos do Estado do Pará (Arcon) estabeleceu um cronograma especial de funcionamento para a data.

A concessionária BRT Amazônia, responsável pela administração do serviço, deverá ajustar o número de viagens e a frota em circulação de acordo com a demanda de passageiros ao longo do domingo, garantindo que não haja desabastecimento de linhas nos horários de maior pico de votação.

O g1 também solicitou mais detalhes sobre o esquema de transporte público em Belém, mas não havia obtido resposta da Prefeitura Municipal e do Sindicato das Empresas de Transporte de Passageiros de Belém (Setransbel) até a última atualização da reportagem.

articles.title: Renan Santos, candidato do Missão à Presidência, faz campanha em Santos e na capital paulista | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato defendeu investimentos em infraestrutura para modernizar o maior porto do país, que fica em Santos.
articles.summary: Candidato defendeu investimentos em infraestrutura para modernizar o maior porto do país, que fica em Santos.
articles.body:
O candidato do Missão , Renan Santos , fez campanha em Santos e na capital paulista.

A primeira agenda de campanha de Renan Santos foi no início da tarde, na cidade de Santos, no litoral paulista. O candidato se reuniu com eleitores e defendeu investimentos em infraestrutura para modernizar o maior porto do país, que fica na cidade.

Depois, Renan Santos foi para a cidade de São Paulo. Ele fez uma caminhada pela região central e discursou duas vezes. A última, no Largo São Francisco, onde fica a tradicional Faculdade de Direito da Universidade de São Paulo. Renan Santos fez um balanço da campanha dele nesse primeiro turno:

“É um ciclo, né? A nossa campanha começa oficialmente aqui e se encerra aqui. A minha carreira, eu nem chamo de carreira, mas a minha participação política começa aqui nessa faculdade e eu não digo que ela se encerra aqui. Mas esse ciclo eleitoral, pelo menos do primeiro turno, se encerra aqui. Então, é muito importante vir para esse território, que é um território importantíssimo, que tem a ver não só com a minha história, mas com a história do país”.

Depois do ato no Centro, Renan Santos ainda teve um outro compromisso. O candidato do Missão participou de um podcast.

articles.body:
A influenciadora digital, Eliziane Ferreira Cruz, que interpreta a personagem Bebinha Arueira , surpreendeu internautas ao anunciar o seu casamento, realizado em um cartório de Palmas , região sul do Tocantins, nesta sexta-feira (2).

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

O momento foi celebrado em clima de chuva e reuniu amigos inusitados do casal, incluindo a presença da filha de Eliziane, o cantor Evoney Fernandes e o Sheik Tocantinense.

Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, a influenciadora caminha em direção ao cartório protegida da chuva por um guarda-chuva. No registro, ela afirmou "estou ansiosa, não estava esperando essa produção, por isso que não anunciei que iria casar".

A personagem Bebinha ganhou destaque nacional após participar do reality show Rancho do Maia, comandado por Carlinhos Maia. Desde então, ela se tornou um fenômeno da internet em 2026.

Eliziane Ferreira Cruz se casou no Tocantins — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Eliziane Ferreira Cruz conta que a inspiração veio de outras mulheres que frequentaram um bar que ela empreendeu por 10 anos.

"Tive bar durante 10 anos, e observava os gestos e as mulheres sempre andavam assim: cabelo assanhado, copo na mão, com os vestidos. E bem alegres, igual a Bebinha", conta Eliziane.

Com 3,2 milhões de seguidores e 1 bilhão de visualizações, Bebinha conquista seguidores com vídeos de humor gravados no Tocantins.

Ela relatou, em conversa com o g1 , que a ideia de gravar vídeos irreverentes surgiu ainda na Bahia, estado em que viveu por muitos anos. Agora, aos 34 anos, ela afirma que foi convidada para vir ao Tocantins pelo grupo do fictício Bar do Arueira.

"No interior da Bahia, fui fazer uma brincadeira com a minha filha e ela achou engraçado. Eu postei o vídeo, e viralizou. [...] Eu terminei chegando aqui [no Tocantins], e estou aqui até hoje", explica a humorista.

articles.title: Mais de 2,29 milhões de eleitores do Sul de Minas estão aptos a votar nas eleições deste domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Região reúne 2.294.826 eleitores; Poços de Caldas, Pouso Alegre e Varginha concentram os maiores colégios eleitorais sul-mineiros.
articles.summary: Região reúne 2.294.826 eleitores; Poços de Caldas, Pouso Alegre e Varginha concentram os maiores colégios eleitorais sul-mineiros.
articles.body:
Fila para votação na Igreja Martir São Sebastião, em Varginha, em 2024 — Foto: Júlia Reis

Mais de 2,29 milhões de eleitores do Sul de Minas estão aptos a comparecer às urnas neste domingo (4), durante as eleições de 2026. De acordo com dados da Justiça Eleitoral, a região reúne 2.294.826 eleitores habilitados para votar na escolha de presidente da República, governador, senador, deputados federais e deputados estaduais.

O g1 acompanha o dia de votação no 1º turno das eleições no Sul de Minas em Tempo Real a partir das 7h deste domingo.

Do total de eleitores, 1.925.549 pessoas estão na faixa em que o voto é obrigatório. Outros 369.277 eleitores pertencem a grupos para os quais o comparecimento às urnas é facultativo, como jovens de 16 e 17 anos e pessoas com 70 anos ou mais.

Entre os maiores colégios eleitorais do Sul de Minas, Poços de Caldas lidera com 122.471 eleitores aptos a votar. Em seguida aparecem Pouso Alegre, com 112.014, e Varginha, com 104.305 eleitores. Juntos, os três municípios somam mais de 338 mil votantes.

Eleições: Fila de eleitores no Univás Campus Fátima, em Pouso Alegre, em 2024 — Foto: Iago Almeida

O perfil do eleitorado regional também revela diversidade entre as faixas etárias. O grupo de 40 a 44 anos é o mais representativo, com 215.927 eleitores. Entre os mais jovens, são 5.372 eleitores de 16 anos e 10.186 de 17 anos aptos a participar do pleito.

Entre os eleitores idosos, o Sul de Minas reúne mais de 316 mil pessoas com 70 anos ou mais. Desse total, 8.323 são centenários habilitados a votar.

Os dados da Justiça Eleitoral mostram ainda que 1.558.401 eleitores da região já possuem biometria cadastrada. O levantamento aponta também a existência de 26.701 eleitores com deficiência e 441 pessoas registradas com nome social.

Neste domingo, os brasileiros irão às urnas para escolher presidente da República, governadores, senadores, deputados federais e deputados estaduais. A votação ocorre das 8h às 17h, no horário de Brasília.

A orientação é que os eleitores confiram previamente o local de votação e levem um documento oficial com foto. O aplicativo e-Título também pode ser utilizado para identificação, desde que contenha fotografia.

Caso nenhum candidato à Presidência da República ou aos governos estaduais alcance a maioria necessária dos votos válidos, o segundo turno será realizado em 25 de outubro.

Para evitar transtornos no dia da votação, a recomendação é verificar antecipadamente a seção eleitoral, separar o documento de identificação e conferir a ordem de votação dos cargos em disputa. A Justiça Eleitoral também orienta os eleitores a evitarem deixar o comparecimento às urnas para os últimos horários do dia, especialmente em cidades com maior movimentação de pessoas nas seções eleitorais.

articles.body:
Augusto Cury , do Avante , fez campanha em Colina, interior paulista.

Augusto Cury visitou a cidade de Colina, onde nasceu, no interior de São Paulo. Ele fez uma caminhada pelo Centro da cidade. A caminhada terminou em frente ao escritório e comitê do Avante na cidade. Augusto Cury disse que pretende focar no empreendedorismo e na educação como forma de aumentar a renda das famílias e alavancar o desenvolvimento do país:

“O brasileiro perdeu a esperança e perdeu a capacidade de sonhar. Então, eu espero, honestamente dizendo, que, através de chamar os melhores especialistas, os melhores gestores, nós possamos desenvolver o país como nunca desenvolveu e ter uma nação que abraça 210 milhões de brasileiros”.

Augusto Cury ainda participou de um almoço com parentes, amigos e empresários da cidade. Depois, seguiu para Ribeirão Preto para descansar, sem compromissos de agenda.

articles.title: Martin O'Hagan: Murder of journalist 25 years on - why has no one been caught?
articles.summary: Martin O'Hagan was shot dead as he walked home from a pub with his wife in Lurgan, County Armagh in 2001. His killers have never been caught.
articles.body:
The brother of a journalist, who was shot dead as he walked home with his wife, says if he did not continue to fight for answers around the murder "the guilt would kill me".

Earlier this week marked the 25th anniversary of the 2001 murder of investigative reporter Martin O'Hagan.

The 51-year-old died in Lurgan, County Armagh, and was shot when walking home from a pub - a killing that was claimed by the Red Hand Defenders, a cover name used by both the Loyalist Volunteer Force and Ulster Defence Association.

But while his murder received widespread condemnation, and numerous charges that were subsequently withdrawn, no one has ever been convicted.

Those close to Martin have said pledges from police and government officials to find those responsible have gone unfulfilled, and they remain frustrated that his death has not received the same recognition as other high profile killings.

Martin was the first person to be murdered for being a journalist in Northern Ireland since the outbreak of the Troubles in 1969.

As a reporter for the Sunday World newspaper, he had built a reputation for stories which exposed paramilitaries and drug dealers operating in Northern Ireland.

He had infuriated County Armagh paramilitary bosses, particularly murdered LVF leader Billy Wright who he labelled 'King Rat ', by exposing crime and drugs rackets.

His brother Fintan told BBC News NI there was "talk that he was digging into collusion, digging into the finances of the LVF but there was never any proof".

"At the time I believed they did it because Martin made a mistake moving up there on the outskirts of Mourneview, a loyalist estate.

"Martin said at the time: 'the war is over'. It's all very well wishful thinking but at the end of the day it was a foolish thing to do. He made it easy for them and that's a very hard thing to live with," Fintan said.

"Within a short period of time the police were assuring us they were going to catch them" and "we, like fools, believed them".

Fintan now says he believes the people who murdered Martin were British agents.

In 2022, security sources told a BBC Spotlight investigation that police were given names of people said to have been involved in the killing within 48 hours but did not act on the information.

Fintan said, given the extensive surveillance of the Mid Ulster LVF, to believe that the intelligence service did not know Martin's murder was being planned is "just unbelievable".

He said the family have flagged a number of details about the case with the Police Ombudsman's office and if they are not included in the upcoming report then it's "not worth the paper it's written on".

He said while he is "hopeful", the family have had so many disappointments they do not get their hopes built up and deal with it in a "business-like fashion".

"It will come out, whether or not it confirms everything that I have experienced and seen and read – I doubt it."

In a statement, the Ombudsman's office said that since her appointment as new Police Ombudsman in June, Jacqui Durkin has been in contact with the O'Hagan family and "assured them that the completion of the public statement is one of her early priorities".

"She is actively reviewing the draft public statement and will provide the family with a publication timeline in due course."

A UK government spokesperson said Martin's murder was a "horrific attack on freedom of speech" and urged anyone with information to contact police.

"The safety of journalists is paramount," they added. "The UK government remains steadfastly committed to ensuring journalists are able to carry out their work free from threat, intimidation, or violence."

Martin had a history of involvement in the Official IRA (the group from which the Provisional IRA would emerge) and spent five years in Long Kesh prison in the early 1970s for moving weapons.

Fintan said he turned his back on violence when he got out of prison, got his degree and became a journalist.

"I think the fact that Martin had been in jail and in the Official IRA, which is no secret, I think that affected things," said Fintan.

"The first journalist [to be murdered in Northern Ireland], the flag bearers of free speech and the right to know is journalism, and it didn't really catch fire the way it should have, and I think it was his background of being a working-class republican," Fintan said.

"If you can't protect your journalists there's no such thing as news or free speech."

Richard Sullivan worked alongside Martin at the Sunday World and said the then Secretary of State John Reid stood in their offices and pledged that they would catch his killers and "no stone would be left un-turned in pursuing them".

"He also said that he would ensure that journalists would be able to work in Northern Ireland free from threat.

"Yet journalists continue to be threatened, even right up to this current day. And obviously, 25 years, a quarter of a century after Marty was killed, there's no sign of a prosecution," Sullivan said.

Martin's case has been contrasted with the murder of journalist Veronica Guerin in Dublin five years previously.

She had written several exposés of organised crime in Dublin and had been subjected to threats and beatings.

Within a week of her murder, the Irish government enacted the Proceeds of Crime Act 1996 and the Criminal Assets Bureau Act 1996, so that assets purchased with money obtained through crime could be seized by the government, leading to the formation of the Criminal Assets Bureau (CAB).

Brian Meehan was convicted for his role in the murder of Guerin.

"Dublin was in the grips of an organised crime war. And Veronica did an awful lot of reporting and covering of that. She was a victim of a contract killing," Sullivan said.

"And in a very similar way, that's what happened to Marty. But in Veronica's case, the government and security force reaction down there was like night and day to what happened up here.

"If a journalist was gunned down and shot on the streets as he walked home after a drink with his wife in London or Manchester or Liverpool, you would never hear the end of it, they would move heaven and earth to have the law changed to get these people caught.

"But in Marty's case, the investigation just fizzled out and stopped, even though they say the case is still open.

"Nothing has happened, and there's no sign of anything happening in the near future. The contrast couldn't be greater," Sullivan said.

Fintan will continue to fight for answers for what happened to his older brother.

"What I'm doing is not just for Martin, it's for me because if I wasn't doing anything the guilt would kill me for not doing something for my brother, and this is really the only thing I can do."

However, he said the more time passes the less likely that will happen.

"If you have an inquiry that's not being done properly or running into obstacles and the longer it goes on the less people care; the only people who care are family, close friends and colleagues.

"If the state's involved, which I'm convinced they are with what I've seen, why would they move heaven and earth to find the culprits?"

In a statement, the PSNI said they "continue to appeal anyone who has information about those responsible for this heinous act to do the right thing and tell us what they know".

"As this matter is currently subject to an ongoing Police Ombudsman investigation, it would be inappropriate to comment further."

articles.title: Eleitorado da região de Ribeirão Preto: raio-x revela perfil | G1
articles.standfirst: Em 66 cidades, mais de 1,8 milhão de pessoas são esperadas para escolha de presidente, governador, deputados e senadores. Em queda em 43 municípios, eleitorado recuou o equivalente a uma cidade do tamanho de São Joaquim da Barra.
articles.summary: O eleitorado da região de Ribeirão Preto recuou 2,6%, com cidades registrando mais votantes que moradores e um aumento significativo de eleitores acima de 60 anos.
articles.body:
A 70 quilômetros de Franca (SP), a estância turística de Rifaina (SP) espera 5,1 mil pessoas nas urnas neste domingo (4). São quase 1 mil a mais que as registradas como moradoras, segundo o IBGE. Enquanto isso, em Cássia dos Coqueiros (SP), a 78 quilômetros de Ribeirão Preto (SP), um em cada três eleitores habilitados pela Justiça Eleitoral tem 60 anos ou mais.

Curiosidades como essas ajudam a entender o perfil do eleitorado das 66 cidades da região de Ribeirão Preto (SP) que vai movimentar a escolha para presidente, governador de São Paulo, senadores e deputados no primeiro turno.

Um eleitorado que ultrapassa 1,8 milhão, mas que recuou 2,6% em relação ao pleito de 2022, o equivalente a 50,5 mil eleitores, algo próximo à população de uma cidade do porte de São Joaquim da Barra (SP).

Confira, a seguir, um raio-X do eleitorado de 2026 na região de Ribeirão Preto.

Chegada a Cássia dos Coqueiros, SP — Foto: Cacá Trovó/EPTV

📉Desde 2022, 43 das das 66 cidades da região de Ribeirão Preto tiveram queda no número de eleitores. A baixa mais acentuada, de 8,94%, ocorreu proporcionalmente em Santa Rosa de Viterbo (SP), onde mais de 1,7 mil pessoas a menos deixarão de ir às urnas neste domingo.

Em Ituverava (SP) e Igarapava (SP) , as diferenças também chamam atenção. Na primeira cidade, 27,4 mil pessoas devem votar, 2,6 mil a menos do que há quatro anos, uma variação negativa de 8,6%.

Na segunda, são também cerca de 1,7 mil eleitores a menos na comparação com 2022, e uma variação proporcional de 7,9%.

Raio-X das eleições 2026 na região de Ribeirão Preto (SP). — Foto: Arte/g1

📈 As demais 23 cidades tiveram um acréscimo de até 13,8% no eleitorado , realidade de Rifaina (SP).

Santo Antônio da Alegria (SP), Santa Cruz da Esperança (SP), Buritizal (SP), Jeriquara (SP) e Cândido Rodrigues (SP) tiveram altas entre 6,2% e 10,9%.

🗳️Com isso, no saldo geral, a região tem 1.835.060 eleitores, 50.591 a menos na comparação com as eleições presidenciais de 2022.

Eleitores na Adevirp, em Ribeirão Preto (SP). — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Como reflexo das características demográficas da região, as quatro maiores cidades dessa área do estado de São Paulo respondem por quase a metade de todo o eleitorado deste ano .

📌Juntas, Ribeirão Preto (SP), Franca (SP), Sertãozinho (SP) e Barretos (SP) contam com 891.628 eleitores, o que representa 48,5%.

Sozinha, Ribeirão Preto responde por mais de um quarto do eleitorado , com 471.128 pessoas aptas a votar, 3,4 mil a mais com relação ao registrado quatro anos atrás.

Em Franca, são 241.708 eleitores , 5,4 mil a menos do que em 2022. Sertãozinho e Barretos têm, respectivamente, 93.439 e 85.353 eleitores . Nos dois casos, os números são inferiores aos da eleição presidencial passada.

Na outra ponta, os dados da Justiça Eleitoral mostram pelo menos quatro cidades da região com menos de 3 mil eleitores. São elas: Taquaral (SP), Santa Cruz da Esperança (SP), Cássia dos Coqueiros (SP) e Cândido Rodrigues (SP).

Rifaina (SP) tem mais eleitores do que moradores — Foto: EPTV/Reprodução

⁉️Entre as 66 cidades da região, três curiosamente têm mais eleitores do que moradores .

Além de Rifaina , esse é o caso de Santa Cruz da Esperança , onde vivem 2.173 pessoas, segundo a estimativa mais recente do IBGE, mas conta com 2.343 eleitores neste domingo.

A mesma situação é observada em Restinga (SP) , que tem 6.480 habitantes, 349 a menos do que o número total de eleitores habilitados.

Especialistas explicam que um dos motivos é o fluxo migratório : gente que se muda para outra cidade, mas mantém o título eleitoral no município onde vivia antes.

📌A tendência geral de envelhecimento da população também se reflete nas eleições. Em toda a região, praticamente um em cada quatro eleitores já tem 60 anos ou mais, o que representa 474.069 pessoas .

Em cinco municípios, todos com menos de 10 mil habitantes, essa proporção é ainda maior, e está na casa do 30%. São eles: Cássia dos Coqueiros, Cândido Rodrigues, Pirangi , Fernando Prestes e Santo Antônio da Alegria.

Em Ribeirão Preto e Franca, o peso dos 60+ se aproxima disso e responde por 27% do eleitorado, o equivalente a 129.418 e a 66.877 eleitores, respectivamente.

articles.title: Um protocolo para garantir sono de qualidade  | G1
articles.standfirst: Livro do neurocientista Andrew Huberman, professor da faculdade de medicina de Stanford, também dá dicas em outras áreas da saúde, como controle de estresse, foco e crescimento pessoal.
articles.summary: Livro do neurocientista Andrew Huberman, professor da faculdade de medicina de Stanford, também dá dicas em outras áreas da saúde, como controle de estresse, foco e crescimento pessoal.
articles.body:
O que é um protocolo? É uma fórmula estabelecida para superar obstáculos e atingir um objetivo. Isso é o que torna irresistível o recém-lançado Protocolos: um manual operacional do corpo humano (Intrínseca). Escrito por Andrew Huberman, professor de neurociência da Universidade Stanford e apresentador do podcast Huberman Lab , um dos mais populares do mundo, ele é dividido em sete áreas – sono; exercício físico; controle de estresse; nutrição; luz; foco, motivação e aprendizado; e crescimento pessoal – e funciona como um guia com muita informação científica, mas, principalmente, recheado de soluções que podem ser postas em prática.

O neurocientista Andrew Huberman, professor da faculdade de medicina de Stanford e autor de Protocolos: um manual operacional do corpo humano — Foto: Divulgação

“Nenhuma pílula vai substituir atividade física, sono de qualidade e manejo do estresse. Ou seja, não é preciso comprar nada para começar a melhorar sua qualidade de vida”, afirma o autor, que defende que, quando aprendemos a explorar nosso sistema nervoso, podemos alcançar alguns pequenos superpoderes. No entanto, o que me conquistou de saída foi Huberman ter escolhido ancorar seu livro no sono, justificando que ele impacta todos os aspectos da nossa fisiologia e psicologia: “É a base da saúde mental, física e do nosso desempenho”, diz.

Como uma coluna não daria conta de discorrer sobre as quase 600 páginas da obra, decidi abordar sono e estresse, questões que preocupam a maior parte das pessoas. Para o primeiro tema, o neurocientista relacionou 15 protocolos a serem seguidos. Fiz uma pequena seleção que resumo aqui:

Veja a luz do sol o quanto antes: exponha os olhos à luz natural entre os primeiros 30 e 60 minutos depois de acordar, mas sem olhar direto para o sol. Esse primeiro protocolo desencadeia dezenas de processos benéficos que mantêm o cérebro e o corpo em funcionamento ao longo do dia.

Veja a luz do sol no fim do dia: de dez a 15 minutos ao ar livre antes que o sol se ponha ajudam a amenizar os impactos negativos da exposição às luzes artificiais da noite.

Descubra seus horários ideais de sono e se esforce para manter a rotina: um estudo com 700 mil pessoas revelou um vínculo causal entre ser uma pessoa diurna e ter uma saúde mental melhor. O professor sugere tentar dormir às 22h para acordar revigorado às 6h ou mesmo antes. Enfatiza que a quantidade suficiente de sono REM tem relação direta com a longevidade, enquanto a falta dele está associada ao aumento dos riscos de mortalidade. Para quem não lembra da aula de biologia: REM é a última fase do ciclo de sono e se caracteriza por movimentos oculares rápidos, sonhos vívidos e atividade cerebral intensa. É essencial para a memória, o aprendizado e a regulação emocional, repetindo-se várias vezes durante a noite. Huberman propõe o que chama de “alguns truques esquisitos” para dormir. Um exemplo é a “caminhada mental”. Imagine-se indo da cama à porta de casa, depois andando até a rua e voltando. Ocupar o cérebro agitado com uma tarefa fácil pode interromper a ruminação, explica.

Reduza a temperatura corporal central noturna: deixe o ambiente com temperatura baixa, entre 18 e 21 graus. Garanta que seja fácil tirar pés e mãos da coberta, porque as extremidades ajudam a resfriar o corpo – portanto, nunca prenda o lençol nas laterais da cama. E evite meias, que podem interromper o processo de resfriamento.

Adote o repouso profundo sem sono (NSDR, em inglês): trata-se de um relaxamento dirigido que inclui respirar de forma que a duração da exalação seja propositalmente acentuada. Também exige mudar o foco de nossa atenção de uma parte do corpo para outra, de forma sistemática – de lugares próximos a distantes.

Vá com calma nos medicamentos controlados para dormir: todos têm efeitos colaterais e interferem na arquitetura do sono e na função glinfática, que remove subprodutos metabólicos neurotóxicos do sistema nervoso central. Tente superar a insônia com a terapia cognitivo-comportamental.

Ajuste os horários do consumo de cafeína: evite no período de oito a dez horas antes de se deitar.

Evite álcool por pelo menos oito horas antes de dormir: durante a primeira metade da noite, a presença do álcool suprime o sono REM e faz com que demoremos mais para atingir qualquer outro ciclo REM.

Evite a exposição a telas por pelo menos uma hora antes de dormir : é possível reduzir o brilho ou ativar a função de modo noturno de celulares, tablets, notebooks e TVs, ou usar óculos que bloqueiam luz azul e verde (os comprimentos de onda mais curtos).

“O estresse é a tentativa da natureza de criar uma solução única para todos os assuntos”, escreve o neurocientista, ponderando que a arquitetura básica da resposta é sempre a mesma. A saída? Calibrar o sistema nervoso autônomo para que o nível de estresse corresponda ao estressor que enfrentamos – de leve a intenso, de breve a contínuo.

E aqui vão algumas dicas para quando estamos no olho do furacão:

Dê de um a três suspiros profundos fisiológicos : inspire fundo pelo nariz até que os pulmões estejam cheios (a barriga deve se expandir junto). Em seguida, inspire bruscamente uma segunda vez, ainda pelo nariz, para inflar ao máximo os pulmões. Depois expire devagar pela boca até que os pulmões se esvaziem. Repita esse padrão de inspiração e expiração no mínimo três vezes seguidas.

Use a exposição deliberada ao frio para aumentar a tolerância ao estresse: pode ser algo tão simples quanto um banho frio, ou elaborado como um banho de gelo. É possível optar por um protocolo cronometrado (de um a três minutos por sessão); ou de contagem dos “muros de adrenalina” – na prática, quando você sente o impulso de sair do frio e, ainda assim, permanece nele, significa que escalou um muro. Há uma alternativa à exposição ao frio: de três a cinco minutos de hiperventilação cíclica, na qual se inspira longa e vigorosamente pelo nariz e se expira de forma passiva pela boca várias vezes.

Use o repouso profundo sem sono, detalhado anteriormente, em sessões de dez a 30 minutos: é especialmente útil em períodos de alto estresse que duram semanas ou mais.

Faça uma micromeditação de cinco minutos quando acordar: depois de sair da cama e ir ao banheiro, sente-se ou deite-se e fique o mais imóvel possível enquanto se concentra na respiração. Observe para onde sua mente vai e leve o foco de volta para a respiração – inspirações e expirações lentas, pelo nariz, são as melhores.

Aumente seu pico matinal de cortisol e catecolaminas: combine de três a quatro ações, como se expor à luz solar; hidratar-se bebendo de meio litro a um litro de água e consumir um pouco de cafeína nas primeiras duas horas do dia; praticar exercícios pela manhã; seguir um dos protocolos de exposição ao frio.

articles.title: Cornell president vows transparency amid outrage over fraternity rape case
articles.summary: Michael Kotlikoff expresses deep sorrow over the case, calling it one of the most challenging periods for Cornell.
articles.body:
Cornell University’s president, Michael Kotlikoff, has called the alleged 2024 gang rape of a student at a fraternity house “deeply disturbing”, pledging greater transparency amid mounting outrage over how the school handled the case.

“My heart aches when I think of what she experienced,” Kotlikoff said in an eight-minute video message to the Cornell community on Saturday.

He characterised the past week as one of the most difficult in the university’s history and said it would weigh on the university for years to come. “It raises heartbreaking and troubling issues about sexual assault, dehumanisation and aspects of party culture, alcohol and drug use,” he said.

The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, alleges she was sexually assaulted by multiple members of the Chi Phi fraternity in 2024 and has sued the university and seven former students.

Scrutiny over Cornell’s handling of the case intensified after New York Governor Kathy Hochul said newly released information had undermined her confidence in the local prosecutor, who initially declined to bring charges.

Hochul subsequently appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to take over the criminal investigation, saying she would “not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug”.

The case has also renewed scrutiny of the “ voluntary intoxication loophole ” in New York law that makes it difficult to prosecute sexual assaults involving victims who voluntarily consumed alcohol or drugs, even if they later became too intoxicated to consent.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten had cited the legal provision in defending his original decision not to pursue charges. Hochul has pledged to push for changes to it.

At a student assembly hearing on Thursday, several speakers called for Kotlikoff’s resignation.

In Saturday’s video, Kotlikoff reaffirmed his support for an independent review of the university’s handling of the case and said Cornell’s Board of Trustees would announce details next week. He also called for a “serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life”.

James’s appointment has placed the case under a prosecutor whose office has repeatedly clashed with President Donald Trump. She has separately described the case as “an active criminal investigation”.

articles.title: Texas mother facing capital murder charges after allegedly shooting her two sons to death
articles.summary: Colleen Nichole Lemmon allegedly told officers she shot both her sons at their Waxahachie home before deputies found her with self-inflicted injuries.
articles.body: A Texas mother is facing capital murder charges after allegedly shooting her two sons before appearing to harm herself, authorities said. Colleen Nichole Lemmon, 42, was taken into custody and charged with two counts of capital murder, according to the Ellis County Sheriff's Office. Authorities said they received a call about an "unknown emergency" just before 4:15 a.m. Thursday on Big Sky Drive in Waxahachie. Upon arriving at the scene, deputies discovered two male victims with gunshot wounds inside the residence. ILLINOIS MOTHER CHARGED WITH MURDER IN DEATH OF 2-YEAR-OLD SON IN CASE DRAWING COMPARISONS TO LINDSAY CLANCY Christopher Scott Pitre, 21, was pronounced dead at the scene. The second victim, a 15-year-old boy, was taken to a hospital in critical condition, where he later died. Deputies said they also found Lemmon suffering from non-life-threatening injuries. Evidence recovered during the investigation gave law enforcement probable cause to believe Lemmon was responsible for shooting both of her children. DAYS AFTER LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL, ANOTHER MASSACHUSETTS MOM ACCUSED OF KILLING HER CHILDREN SEEKS FREEDOM Deputies found Lemmon covered in blood with what appeared to be self-inflicted lacerations on her wrists and a handgun nearby, according to an arrest affidavit obtained by FOX 4. Lemmon allegedly told officers, "I shot both my kids." She was arrested and transported to a local hospital for treatment, authorities said. Scott Pitre, the boys' father, told NBC 5 that his younger son had recently celebrated his 15th birthday. He said he wants justice for his sons. LINDSAY CLANCY'S THREE CHILD VICTIMS FORGOTTEN AMID CROWDS OF SUPPORT: MOTHER OF SIX Ida Brown, a neighbor, described the killings as "heartbreaking." "It's heartbreaking, and I'm praying for them," she told FOX 4. Sheriff Brad Norman offered his condolences to the family. "My deepest sympathies go out to the victims' father, family members, and loved ones involved in this tragic incident," Norman said in a statement. "They will remain in our prayers during this difficult time." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Lemmon is being held on a $2.5 million bond.

articles.title: Shooting near Baltimore youth football event leaves 12-year-old girl dead, 3 adults wounded
articles.summary: A parking dispute near a youth football event at Leon Day Park in Baltimore turned deadly when two men allegedly opened fire on each other, killing a 12-year-old girl in the crossfire.
articles.body: A 12-year-old girl was killed and three adults were wounded after two gunmen allegedly opened fire during a dispute near a youth football game in Baltimore, Maryland, authorities said Saturday. The preteen girl was apparently caught in the crossfire at Leon Day Park, where a youth football league was holding its homecoming event, Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley said during a news conference. The two men are believed to have been in a dispute that started over a parking space, according to Worley. "What we know is that there was some type of argument between two cowards, and of course, they both opened fire on each other," Worley said. PANTHERS GREAT JONATHAN STEWART EXPLAINS WHY YOUTH SPORTS MATTER FAR BEYOND THE FIELD "In the crossfire, a 12-year-old little girl who was probably down there watching football was shot and killed," he added. As of Saturday evening, police said they were searching for at least two suspects, whom authorities described as adult men. No arrests had been announced as of late Saturday night. Baltimore police told Fox News Digital that officers responded to the 1200 block of North Franklintown Road at approximately 6:15 p.m. after receiving multiple reports of gunfire. Officers found a 25-year-old woman suffering from an apparent gunshot wound and the 12-year-old girl, who was transported to a hospital but later pronounced dead. LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY PARK SHOOTING KILLS 1, INJURES 4 DURING LIVE BAND PERFORMANCE A 28-year-old man and a 23-year-old man separately walked into area hospitals seeking treatment for gunshot wounds, police said. All three surviving victims were listed in stable condition. Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott gave an emotionally charged reaction to the incident, which he said unfolded because two adults couldn't resolve an argument without guns. "Two grown men got into an argument and now a 12-year-old is gone," he said. AT LEAST 3 DEAD, 23 WOUNDED IN SEPARATE MASS SHOOTINGS LESS THAN 15 MINUTES APART "What happened out here today is one of the most disgusting things I've ever seen in my life," Scott added. Scott said the girl's death would have a profound impact on the community before offering his condolences to her family. "We're never gonna see her full potential," he said. "Her family's gonna be hurting for this for the rest of their life. Her classmates are going to be hurting, her community's going to be hurting." articles.title: Trump, crime and corruption loom over Brazil’s presidential vote
articles.summary: Brazilians will vote in a general election on Sunday with two familiar political camps once again dominating the presidential race.
articles.body: Millions of Brazilians will vote in a general election on Sunday that will choose the country’s president against a backdrop of corruption scandals, deep political polarization and growing voter fatigue, with two familiar political camps once again dominating the race. Among the frontrunners are the country’s leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of imprisoned former President Jair Bolsonaro, who are championing different paths for Brazil. “It’s two competing visions of what the country should look like and what Latin America should look like,” Brian Winter, editor-in-chief of Americas Quarterly and vice president of policy at Americas Society/Council of the Americas, told CNN. Voting is compulsory for most adults in the world’s fifth largest country, and turnout is typically among the highest in the Americas. The choice facing Brazilians extends well beyond domestic politics and could reshape how Brazil positions itself on the global stage. The vote would determine whether the region’s largest country tilts toward a growing conservative bloc aligned with US President Donald Trump or continues Lula’s pursuit of a multipolar foreign policy. Lula, 80, is seeking a fourth and likely last term. He governed Brazil from 2003 to 2010 and returned to the presidency in 2023 after a remarkable political comeback: Lula spent 580 days in prison on corruption convictions that Brazil’s Supreme Court later annulled in 2021, restoring his political rights, before he defeated then-president Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election. Lula is neck and neck with Flávio, who is trying to carry forward the political movement built around his father. Jair Bolsonaro, now under humanitarian house arrest for health reasons, is barred from running and is serving a 27-year sentence after being convicted of attempting a coup to overturn his 2022 election loss. Four other presidential hopefuls trail behind Lula and the younger Bolsanaro in the polls. They include centrist psychiatrist and best-selling author Augusto Cury; right-wing former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado; Renan Santos, a right-wing founder of the Movimento Brasil Livre now running under the Missão party; and Romeu Zema, the economically liberal, right-leaning former governor of the state of Minas Gerais. If no candidate wins more than half of valid votes on Sunday, the two with the most votes advance to an October 25 runoff. Two visions of Brazil’s place in the world Lula has continued to champion multilateralism while distancing the country from the United States. That shift is visible in Brazil’s official trade data. China has been Brazil’s biggest export market since 2009, but its lead has widened sharply since Trump came to power. Lula’s relationship with Trump soured as Brazil became caught up in the US president’s tariff agenda and US policy toward organized crime in Latin America — friction that has given Lula another platform to run on: Brazil’s sovereignty. The first flashpoint came in summer of 2025, when Trump announced tariffs on many Brazilian goods, while explicitly citing what his administration called the politically motivated prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro. The tariffs were later rolled back in November. The former Brazilian president’s other son, Eduardo Bolsonaro, who moved to the US and lobbied the Trump administration on his father’s behalf, initially claimed credit for the pressure — a boast that later backfired on Flávio’s campaign as the tariffs hurt Brazilian businesses. Trade tensions returned this summer when Trump imposed fresh tariffs on certain Brazilian goods, still in effect today. Lula rejected the measures and threatened to retaliate against the US — a move he said later in September, in an interview with CNN’s Christiane Amanpour, he would hold off on while negotiations with Washington continued. The ongoing spat with the US has resonated with swing voters who lean right and embrace nationalist ideals. “Some have joked that the most effective campaigner for Lula has been Donald Trump,” Winter said. “The tariffs and the other efforts to interfere in Brazil’s politics have, for the most part, backfired and helped Lula.” Lula brought that argument onto the world stage at the United Nations General Assembly in September. “Brazil is nobody’s backyard,” he said, while accusing “some Brazilian politicians” of aligning themselves with foreign interests at odds with the country’s own — remarks widely seen as aimed at Flávio Bolsonaro. That divide extends to other foreign relations: Two days after Lula’s UN speech, Brazilian diplomats joined representatives of several countries in walking out as Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began his address, amid Lula’s sharpening criticism of Israel’s conduct in Gaza. Flávio Bolsonaro has taken a markedly different approach, cultivating ties with Netanyahu, Trump and other leaders Lula has clashed with. When Flávio launched his campaign in July, Netanyahu appeared by video to endorse him, as reported by CNN Brasil. In May, Flávio met Trump in the Oval Office to discuss organized crime, tariffs and critical minerals, then Vance and Rubio the next day. Argentine President Javier Milei, a libertarian and longtime Bolsonaro-family ally, traveled to Brazil in July to back Flávio’s campaign. He called Lula a “convict” and the government “thieving socialists,” prompting Brazil to recall its ambassador to Buenos Aires. This comes as Latin America’s broader political map has moved right following closely fought elections: Right-wing firebrand Abelardo de la Espriella narrowly won Colombia’s presidential election in June, and Keiko Fujimori won Peru’s runoff weeks later by roughly a tenth of a percentage point. “A Flávio Bolsonaro victory would cement this move to the right that we’ve seen in so much of Latin America over the last two years,” Winter said, noting that many of the region’s right-leaning governments are aligned with Trump on security and drug policy. Crime at the forefront That alignment intersects with voters’ most immediate concern: crime. “Security and crime have been the main issues that have led the Latin American right to win 13 of the last 16 presidential elections in Latin America,” Winter said, noting that robberies, extortion and cellphone theft still shape how Brazilians experience insecurity even as homicide rates have fallen over the past decade. Much like his father, Flávio has made a tougher approach to crime central to his campaign, advocating for the designation of major criminal factions as terrorist organizations, new federal prisons and lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 16. “The family’s brand has been successful above all because they’re seen as intolerant of crime,” Winter said, pointing to Jair Bolsonaro’s signature finger-gun pose. During his May trip to Washington, Flávio urged the Trump administration to classify Brazil’s two most powerful criminal organizations as terrorist groups; the US announced days later that the designation would take effect that June. Lula’s government opposed the move, warning that applying a terrorism framework to Brazilian criminal groups could become a pretext for foreign intervention. Affordability and an uneasy electorate Brazilians are also grappling with a slowing economy and persistent affordability issues. Headline indicators show low unemployment and moderating inflation, yet perceptions of household finances remain far less upbeat. “The economy is OK, but people feel like their salary doesn’t go as far,” Winter said. “They feel like their standard of living has declined, even when sometimes the official statistics tell a different story.” These cost-of-living concerns loom over Lula’s record. The leader is associated with social mobility and poverty reduction in Brazil, which was fueled by a booming economy during his first two terms, from 2003 to 2010. But this time, many voters are struggling to feel a similar jump. “The progress has not been nearly as widely felt as it was during his first two terms,” Winter said. Flávio faces a different challenge: inheriting a movement still centered on his father while presenting himself as his own candidate. “Flavio Bolsonaro is not the Bolsonaro that most right-wing voters originally wanted to cast a ballot for,” Winter said. “He is clearly the most moderate member of the family, and that may give him appeal to swing voters, but it also means that he doesn’t stir enthusiasm in the same way that his father did.” Women are an important part of that challenge. “The new right has struggled with women voters, not just in Brazil, but throughout the Americas,” Winter said. Flávio’s campaign has given his wife, Fernanda Bolsonaro, a more visible role in an effort to appeal to women voters — but a public rupture with his stepmother Michelle Bolsonaro, a prominent evangelical figure who had helped Jair Bolsonaro make inroads with conservative women, complicated that effort. Although the two reconciled, Flávio is still struggling to make ground with that base. “There’s a real gender divide,” Winter said. Religion is another crucial fault line in Brazil, where Catholic and evangelical voters remain politically important. Datafolha’s latest poll shows Flávio leading Lula among evangelical voters, 47% to 27%, while Lula leads among Catholics, 45% to 33%. An ‘apathetic polarization’ The vote comes at a time of deep polarization among the electorate, who are slower to engage than in previous races. “The polarization continues to organize the race, but it is mobilizing the electorate with less intensity,” said Felipe Nunes, a political scientist and CEO of polling institute Quaest. Winter described it as an “apathetic polarization,” where Brazilians “are still wearing the shirt of their team, politically speaking … but they’re doing it without much enthusiasm.” That contrasts with Brazil’s last two elections. Bolsonaro rose to power in 2018 amid recession, crime and the fallout from a sweeping corruption probe centered on a bribery scheme at state oil giant Petrobras that implicated politicians and business leaders across the spectrum and badly damaged Lula’s Workers’ Party. By 2022, Lula narrowly beat Bolsonaro amid criticism of Bolsonaro’s handling of the pandemic and fears for the country’s democracy. Corruption across the political divide Much of this year’s fatigue traces back to a sense of hopelessness over systemic corruption, which ranks among voters’ biggest concerns, yet neither camp can claim the issue as its own, say experts. Brasília has been consumed for months by investigations surrounding the collapse of Brazilian bank Banco Master and its former chief executive, Daniel Vorcaro, whose relationships extended across Brazil’s political, financial and judicial establishment. Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, one of Bolsonarism’s main adversaries, has become a central figure in the scandal. Moraes has long been portrayed by Bolsonaro supporters as aligned with Lula for his role in the investigations that led to the former president’s coup conviction. The issue has been pounced upon by Flávio on the election campaign when the court began weighing whether to investigate claims that Moraes advised Vorcaro as he tried to save Banco Master from collapse, while a law firm run by Moraes’ wife held a three-year, R$131 million (about $25 million) contract with the bank. Moraes has denied wrongdoing; a decision on a formal probe was postponed in September. But as investigators reviewed Vorcaro’s messages, the scandal spread to Flávio’s own campaign. He is now under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering related to financing Vorcaro provided for “Dark Horse,” a film about Jair Bolsonaro. Flávio has denied wrongdoing. Winter said the scandal may be reinforcing dissatisfaction with the political system rather than clearly helping one side: “It reinforces the disgust and apathy that Brazilians feel with their political system as a whole,” he said. For Bruno Brandão, executive director of Transparency International Brazil, the problem goes beyond Banco Master. “One side only cares about the corruption of the other side and closes its eyes to corruption among those in its own political camp,” Brandão told CNN, arguing that polarization makes sustained pressure for accountability harder. He also points to a structural shift, with presidents weakened by successive crises ceding more control over spending to Congress — making this year’s simultaneous congressional elections, which will decide who the next president governs with, especially consequential.

articles.title: Delhi protest row: 3 women journalists allege sexual harassment, complaints sent to Crime Branch
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has transferred complaints from three female journalists alleging sexual harassment during a protest in the New Delhi area on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has transferred complaints from three female journalists alleging sexual harassment during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3 to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.The complaints were received by the New Delhi district police amid what it described as an "emergent law and order situation" during the protest."On 03-10-26, during the protest in the New Delhi area, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists in the context of the emergent law and order situation. New Delhi District has received their complaints and the same are transferred to Crime Branch, Kamla Market for further action," Delhi Police said in a post on X.The Crime Branch at Kamla Market will examine the complaints and take further action based on the allegations, police said.The complaints came amid protests in the capital demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Protesters detained at Jantar MantarAround 150 people were detained in and around Jantar Mantar on Saturday as security forces prevented protesters from gathering at the site.Those detained included senior advocates Prashant Bhushan and Kapil Sibal, Swaraj India founder Yogendra Yadav and AISA national president Neha Bora.AISA also alleged that women protesters, journalists and lawyers were manhandled by male police personnel during the demonstration. TOI reported that a video circulating on social media showed a male police officer grabbing Bora from behind while detaining her. Police have not responded to those allegations.CJP spokesperson alleges journalist was sexually assaultedThe complaints by the three journalists also come amid allegations raised by CJP spokesperson Saurav Das against Delhi Police.Das accused the police of refusing to register an FIR against ACP Vivek Bhagat over the alleged sexual assault of an independent journalist.He said he and CJP leader Ratna Singh had approached the police and demanded that an FIR be registered. Das also warned that journalists and protesters would return to the police station if the case was not registered.Dipke announces October 10 protestMeanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced another protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10 if Gyanesh Kumar does not resign.The announcement followed the CJP's October 2 protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park, where thousands gathered despite police denying permission. Dipke has described the proposed Delhi demonstration as "Jantar Mantar 2.0" and said it would be peaceful.The CJP has been demanding Kumar's resignation over its allegations concerning electoral-roll revisions and the SIR exercise. The allegations have not been independently verified.Police conduct under scrutinyThe latest complaints add to scrutiny of police conduct during the protests.Delhi Police had registered three FIRs over the October 2 demonstrations, while hundreds of protesters were detained as they attempted to reach Jantar Mantar.The three journalists' complaints will now be examined by the Crime Branch.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Japan PM protests to US after Marine arrested on suspicion of murder in Okinawa
articles.summary: A US Marine was arrested Sunday on suspicion of murder and robbery after a woman’s body was discovered in a hotel room in Japan, prompting the country’s prime minister to express her outrage to the US over the alleged incident she called “ extremely brutal and heinous.”
articles.body: A US Marine was arrested Sunday on suspicion of murder and robbery after a woman’s body was discovered in a hotel room in Japan, prompting the country’s prime minister to express her outrage to the US over the alleged incident she called “ extremely brutal and heinous.” A 39-year-old woman was found unresponsive in her hotel room in Naha city on Okinawa island and pronounced dead at the scene early Saturday, Okinawa police said. “The Government of Japan has strongly protested to the U.S. side and has called for the fullest possible cooperation with the investigation, thorough discipline among U.S. military personnel, and comprehensive measures to prevent the recurrence of crimes and accidents,” Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said in a statement on X. Police told CNN that based on the condition of the woman’s body, she appeared to have been murdered, but did not provide any more details. The 20-year-old Marine was stationed at Futenma Air Station, also on the island, police added. CCTV footage reportedly showed a man, believed to be a foreign national, with a shaved head, entering the hotel room with the woman and later leaving the building with her belongings in hand, police said. In a statement, the US Marine Corps extended condolences to the victim’s family and said it takes the allegations “very seriously and expects every Marine to adhere to the highest standards of behavior.” “We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force,” it said. The US embassy in Tokyo said on X it was “aware that a US service member is in custody following the death of a Japanese national in Okinawa.” “As an investigation is underway to determine the facts of the case, the United States is communicating and cooperating with the Government of Japan and local authorities,” the embassy added. The woman’s body was discovered at around 4.30 am local time on Saturday and the US Marine was arrested less than 24 hours later, at 1am local time, while walking around the city, the force added. Police said an investigation is ongoing. Despite Okinawa’s importance to US military strategy, the US troops stationed on the island have at times caused resentment and anger among residents. In 1995, the rape of a 12-year-old girl by three US servicemen unleashed outrage and mass protests in Okinawa.

articles.title: Bosnia general election 2026 explained in maps and charts
articles.summary: Bosnians head to the polls on October 4. Here’s a quick guide to the voting process, candidates and what’s at stake.
articles.body:
Bosnians are heading to the polls to choose the next government at all three of the state, entity and canton levels. It may seem complicated, but for a country divided into two entities – the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska, along with Brcko District – this is nothing new.

The general elections are scheduled for Sunday, October 4. More than 3.4 million people are eligible to vote.

This year, new election technology will be used. Voters will be identified using biometric devices, while ballot papers will be scanned rather than simply placed in ballot boxes.

The use of scanners, however, does not mean voting will be fully electronic. Votes will still be cast and recorded on paper, but verification and counting should be faster and more transparent, while voter identification should be more accurate.

Candidates for the Bosniak representative include current Presidency member Denis Becirovic of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Bakir Izetbegovic of the Party of Democratic Action (SDA), Semir Efendic of the Party for Bosnia and Herzegovina (Stranka za BiH), and Fahrudin Radoncic of the Union for a Better Future of BiH (SBB).

Izetbegovic, the president of the centre-right SDA, the biggest Bosniak party in the country, is running for his third term after being defeated by Becirovic in 2022.

Three candidates will run for the Croat seat in the Presidency: Darijana Filipovic of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina (HDZ BiH), Slaven Kovacevic of the Democratic Front (DF), and Zdenko Lucic, a candidate supported by a coalition of five Croat parties.

The current Serb member of the Presidency, Zeljka Cvijanovic from the right-wing Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD), is running for a second term. During her term on the country’s top state body, which began in November 2022, just a few months after Russia’s war in Ukraine started, she maintained close and continuous cooperation with Russia and its president, Vladimir Putin.

SNSD is led by Milorad Dodik, the former president of Republika Srpska, best known for his separatist moves and for challenging the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the decisions of former High Representative Christian Schmidt.

Cvijanovic will face Marinko Bozovic of the Serb Democratic Party (SDS) and Nebojsa Vukanovic of the List for Justice and Order.

Voters will be choosing representatives for 14 governments, as well as members of the country’s three-member Presidency.

Each entity has its own president, assembly, prime minister and ministers. The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina is further divided into 10 cantons, each with its own government.

For all this to happen, the Central Election Commission (CIK), the main body responsible for overseeing the voting process, earlier said that 75 political parties and four independent candidates were registered and eligible to participate.

When registered voters go to the polls, they do not elect one president, but choose one of three members of the country’s collective head of state. They are the representatives of the three constituent peoples – Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs.

The Bosniak and Croat members are elected from the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, while the Serb member is elected from Republika Srpska.

This is because the majority of Bosniaks and Croats live in the Federation, while most Serbs live in Republika Srpska.

The election of the Croat member has weighed on Bosniak-Croat relations for years and has often been used as a reason for political blockades.

Parties gathered around the centre-right Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina (HDZ BiH) are demanding changes to the Election Law, saying they want to prevent Bosniak voters from influencing the election of the Croat member of the Presidency.

But that would also require changes to the Constitution, which allows all citizens in the Federation to choose whether they want to vote for the Bosniak or the Croat member.

What about citizens who live outside their constituent group’s voting area?

A Serb living in the Federation, or a Bosniak or Croat living in Republika Srpska, who wants to run would not be able to do so, nor can they vote for those they consider to be their own representatives.

That is one of the many paradoxes of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s electoral system.

How is the state-level government chosen?

Citizens elect representatives to the Parliamentary Assembly, which consists of two houses.

Forty-two representatives will be elected to the House of Representatives.

Two-thirds are directly elected from the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and one-third from Republika Srpska.

A quorum consists of a majority of all members elected to the House of Representatives.

The second chamber – the House of Peoples – has 15 delegates and is elected indirectly through the institutions. It consists of Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs – five from each group.

The election of entity-level authorities works somewhat differently.

In Republika Srpska, citizens directly elect the National Assembly, as well as the entity president and vice presidents.

They do not directly elect the government – it is confirmed by the National Assembly.

In the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, citizens directly elect the House of Representatives of the Federation Parliament and the cantonal assemblies.

Those cantonal assemblies then elect delegates to the Federation’s House of Peoples.

The president of the Federation, the entity government and the cantonal governments are formed after the elections, through parliamentary majorities and political agreements.

Why is it a challenge to form the government?

It is difficult not only because the electoral system is complex, but also because of the lack of agreement among representatives of the three different ethnic communities.

Frequent blockades and obstruction make decision-making difficult at all levels, even though many politicians invoke the politics of compromise.

Elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina, therefore, are not only about who wins, but about whether a system designed to represent everyone can serve its citizens.

New election technologies might reduce potential fraud, but much more will be needed for the country’s path towards the European Union.

The outcome of the election could unblock, or further slow down, the adoption of key laws needed for the country’s progress towards EU membership.

The EU granted Bosnia and Herzegovina candidate status in December 2022 and opened accession negotiations in 2024.

However, the country’s progress has since been assessed as very limited and slowed by political blockades.

These elections will also be a test for the ruling coalition, which promised to focus on social and economic issues amid the rising cost of living.

The first preliminary results are traditionally published by CIK late on election night, on October 4, and are updated every few hours.

In the days after the elections, CIK gradually enters votes from the remaining polling stations, mobile voting teams, as well as ballots received by mail and from diplomatic and consular missions.

The official results will be known no later than November 20.

articles.title: From 1946, NSW planted South African bitou bush to stabilise coastal sand dunes; decades later it had spread along 46% of the state's coastline and threatened native ecosystems
articles.summary: A plant introduced with a practical purpose along the New South Wales (NSW) coast eventually became a major environmental weed.
articles.body: A plant introduced with a practical purpose along the New South Wales (NSW) coast eventually became a major environmental weed. South African bitou bush was deliberately planted along the NSW coastline between 1946 and 1968 to help stabilise sand dunes, according to the NSW Environment and Heritage department. The fast-growing shrub later spread rapidly and is now found along 46% of the state's coastline, with some infestations extending up to 10 kilometres inland. What was once used to control shifting sand has since become a threat to native coastal vegetation and wildlife, prompting long-running efforts to contain and remove it.A plant brought in to stabilise dunesBitou bush, scientifically known as Chrysanthemoides monilifera subsp. rotundata, is native to South Africa. NSW Environment and Heritage says it is thought to have initially reached Australia in ship ballast before later being deliberately used for dune stabilisation. Its deliberate planting along the NSW coast began in 1946 and continued through 1968. The plant was valued because it grew quickly and could help hold loose coastal sand in place. Historical government documents also record its use to stabilise and revegetate dunes affected by coastal sand mining.Planting took place at a number of coastal locations, including Ballina, Byron Bay, Crescent Head, Iluka, Lake Munmorah, Port Macquarie, Redhead, The Entrance and Tweed Heads. The same characteristics that made bitou bush useful for stabilisation, however, also helped it become difficult to control once it established beyond planted areas.How bitou bush spreadOnce established along the coastline, bitou bush spread through a combination of deliberate planting and natural expansion. The NSW government now records it along 46% of the state's coastline, with the north coast particularly heavily affected. In some locations, the shrub has moved as far as 10 kilometres inland. Bitou bush is capable of growing rapidly and forming dense stands. Rather than simply occupying empty spaces, it can move into existing coastal plant communities and create thick shrub layers.That expansion has changed the character of some dunes, headlands and other coastal habitats. Earlier government assessments described an even wider distribution at different points in time, reflecting differences in surveys, definitions and assessment periods. A NSW Scientific Committee determination in 1999, for example, reported the weed on 90% of the state's sandy coast. The current NSW Environment and Heritage data shows the figure as 46% of the state's coastline.Native plants and animals face pressureThe main environmental concern is not simply the presence of an introduced shrub but what happens when it becomes dominant. According to NSW Environment and Heritage, bitou bush invades coastal heathlands, grasslands, woodlands and forests. It can form dense stands that replace native plants and alter habitats used by native animals. Infestations can also smother vegetation communities found on sand dunes and headlands.The NSW Bitou Threat Abatement Plan identified 157 native plant species, three plant populations and 24 ecological communities as being at risk from bitou bush and boneseed invasion. The plan also identified 24 native animal species potentially threatened by the spread of the weeds. Because of these impacts, the NSW Scientific Committee has listed the invasion of native plant communities by bitou bush and boneseed as a key threatening process affecting native plants and animals.Efforts now focus on containment and restorationManaging the weed is now a long-term conservation task. Bitou bush and the related South African plant boneseed were collectively listed as Weeds of National Significance in 2000. NSW has also developed a Threat Abatement Plan that directs control towards sites where removing the weed can provide the greatest benefit to threatened species and ecological communities.The approach involves more than simply removing individual plants. Control programmes involve government agencies, local authorities, community groups, Aboriginal groups, land managers and bush regenerators. The NSW plan identifies 169 priority sites, alongside northern and southern containment zones intended to limit further spread and protect important native vegetation.Under the NSW Biosecurity Act 2015, specific requirements also apply to bitou bush management. In areas north of Cape Byron and south of Point Perpendicular, eradication is required, while the central coastal distribution is managed through containment measures.The history of bitou bush shows how a species introduced to solve one environmental problem can create another when it spreads beyond its intended role. Decades after it was planted to stabilise NSW sand dunes, the shrub has become widespread enough to require coordinated control, with restoration efforts now aimed at giving native coastal ecosystems space to recover.You use AI every day. articles.title: Dancers captured in 1978 Wolverhampton photograph are reunited
articles.summary: The people captured in a celebrated photograph are reunited nearly 50 years later.
articles.body:
When Vivienne Dawes first saw the photograph of herself dancing on a crowded dance floor almost 50 years ago, it felt like being transported back in time.

Captured at Wolverhampton's Culture Centre in 1978, the image shows her among a group of young people immersed in a night of music and dancing.

At the time, none of them could have known the photograph would become an iconic image that has been viewed across the world and one of photographer Chris Steele-Perkins' most recognised works.

Nor could they have imagined that, decades later, they would be reunited through the photo and finally have their stories told.

"Oh my goodness - oh my, and I do look like me, don't I?" Vivianne said when she saw the image.

She is the central dancer in the photograph and can still remember the atmosphere inside the venue.

She said: "Back then, everybody was doing their own thing, was all dancing, and when the music hit us, we felt no pain.

"At the end of the day, we're showing that we're black sisters enjoying reggae music."

Nearly 50 years after it was taken, the image continues to attract attention, appearing most recently in the V&A East exhibition The Music Is Black: A British Story.

Now it is going on display in its home city of Wolverhampton, at the Grand theatre.

Vivienne said she had no awareness when she was dancing that her photo was being taken.

"If you notice the way we all dance, it's like we were on another planet," she said.

Her dance, as captured in the photo, would also later go on to be recreated in a painting by artist Claudette Johnson , which will also appear in the Wolverhampton exhibition.

"I appreciated the fact that someone could put their time into painting a portrait of me.

"I can't believe I looked so attractive back then, really and truly. I look very lovely."

While the photo has become celebrated over the years, the people captured in it have remained largely anonymous, until now.

For Winston Logan, who appears at the back of the photo on the far left, the image is a reminder of a very different Wolverhampton.

Having arrived in Britain about five years before the photo was taken, he remembers a lack of opportunities for young Black people.

"Life is hard, no entertainment, nowhere to go, no fun," he said.

But the Culture Centre on Clarence Street offered something different, becoming a hub for music, dancing and community.

Looking back, Winston sees the image as a snapshot of a pivotal period in his life.

"This is where it starts, [I] went from unemployment, went from there into training, went from there into industry, construction or whatever, and now I'm passing on my skills.

"Mum and dad didn't get to see that photo or find out about that photo."

"This time, to the present day, my life has, I would say, blown up. Well, I can't hide now, can I?"

In an interview with the Guardian in 2014, Steele-Perkins said he had been commissioned to go to Wolverhampton in 1978 by the Sunday Times magazine as part of a feature marking 10 years since local MP Enoch Powell's "Rivers of Blood" speech.

He described it as a difficult commission, adding that he had not really liked the photo at the time, although it had grown on him since and had become his best-selling print.

An event celebrating the launch of the Wolverhampton exhibition on Sunday is set to reunite several of those pictured in the photo, including Macka B, now an international reggae artist, his brother Owen MacFarlane, Casa Simpson, Lisa Green and Sharon Underwood - all of whom still live in and around the city.

The idea for the exhibition came after staff at Wolverhampton Grand Theatre spotted the photograph while visiting The Music Is Black: A British Story at V&A East.

"It stood out amongst all of the other images," curator Tonia Daley-Campbell said.

She said the photograph seemed to bring the dancefloor back to life.

"You can hear it, you can smell it, you can feel that image.

"We want to put all of the young people that were in that photo dancing, vibing, standing by the sound system, whatever they were doing, front and centre," Daley-Campbell said.

"We're bringing it back home and we're going to make sure that is displayed and everybody will know their name."

The exhibition opens at Wolverhampton Grand Theatre's Encore Lounge on 4 October and will run until 31 October. Admission to the event is free.
