articles.title: Australia investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
articles.summary: State police and the country's security agency are looking into the co-pilot, who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel.
articles.body:
Australian authorities are investigating the links between the country and a Flydubai co-pilot who attempted to take control of a plane travelling to Israel.

The co-pilot is alleged to have attacked the captain with a crash axe during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv before passengers managed to overpower him and successfully take control of the plane.

The Australian authorities have not identified the co-pilot, who has been named by multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times as Hamam al-Hammami.

The prosecutor in the UAE has said it is investigating the incident and any possible motives.

In a statement to the BBC, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed its investigation into "the man's links to Australia".

The investigation involves state police and the country's security agency, it said, adding that an update would be "provided at the appropriate time".

Sources familiar with the case, who have spoken to Australian media, have said the co-pilot was issued a student visa in 2014, and studied in Australia between 2015 and 2017, until he left the country.

The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) said the co-pilot's student visa was cancelled in 2019 as he was no longer enrolled in a course, making him ineligible for it.

Counter-terrorism officials will look at whether the man was radicalised in Australia, the ABC reported.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he was an Omani national.

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September was carrying more than 170 passengers to Israel.

Two and a half hours into its journey, the plane plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) when the Omani co-pilot attacked the pilot with a crash axe , the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.

The pilot flying the plane, Capt Smit Machchhar, described how he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.

Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.

Machchhar, an Indian national, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.

The co-pilot was arrested after the emergency landing and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, according to Netanyahu.

The UAE's attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said on Saturday investigations were under way to establish the circumstances, motives and any links related to the incident.

He said investigations into the incident revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act", according to the country's state news agency.

In the days since the attack more details have come to light about the co-pilot's employment history.

While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training because of concerns over his radical views, and was given another role at Oman's national airline.

It is also known that, from 2020, he was studying on a distance-learning course run by Buckinghamshire New University in the UK.

He graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added he did not take any pilot training at the school.

articles.title: California K-9 Otis helps police seize 440 pounds of cocaine during Alhambra traffic stop
articles.summary: K-9 Otis sniffed out roughly 440 pounds of cocaine during a California traffic stop after the driver's shifting stories raised red flags to responding officers.
articles.body: A California traffic stop took a massive turn when a police K-9 sniffed out approximately 200 kilos, or roughly 440 pounds, of cocaine allegedly packed inside an SUV filled with cardboard boxes, authorities said. The Alhambra Police Department said the incident began after officers conducted a traffic stop along Valley Boulevard near the 710 Freeway. Although authorities did not say what prompted the initial stop, they noticed the driver appeared to have an unusual amount of cargo in his vehicle. "The driver was transporting more cardboard boxes than Amazon on Prime Day," police said in a social media post. "At first, he said he was heading home to Huntington Park from his cousin’s house and that the boxes were not his," police said in the post. But that wasn't the man's only story. articles.title: Debris in engine very likely caused RAF Coningsby Spitfire crash
articles.summary: Sqn Ldr Mark Long was killed when the plane he was flying crashed in a field in May 2024.
articles.body:
Debris which had been present in the carburettor of a Spitfire for decades was "very likely" the cause of a crash in which a pilot died, according to a report.

Sqn Ldr Mark Long was killed when the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (BBMF) plane he was flying crashed in a field in Lincolnshire on 25 May 2024.

A report published by the Ministry of Defence says the debris was responsible for causing fuel starvation, "leading to a loss of thrust required to maintain powered flight".

Just 56 seconds after taking off from RAF Coningsby, witnesses saw the plane turn and plunge to the ground.

Long was flying a Spitfire Mk IX, built in 1944, operated by the RAF's BBMF for commemorative flypasts and displays.

The opening of an inquest heard the provisional cause of his death was head and neck injuries.

The Service Inquiry report said chemical analysis revealed evidence that indicated the debris in the carburettor "had been present for decades".

It said: "The presence of multiple, contradictory publications created ambiguity over the correct procedures for carburettor maintenance.

"The panel assessed that this inconsistency likely led to varying interpretations of how extensively the carburettor should have been dismantled, inspected and cleaned, which was very likely to have reduced the reliability of detecting any debris build-up."

The design of the cockpit and restraint were identified as aggravating factors, but the report acknowledged any structural design change would likely require "significant moderations".

"This would not only affect the historic authenticity of the aircraft but would possibly affect overall airworthiness due to a change in aircraft mass and balance," the report said.

Twenty-six safety recommendations were included in the report, including improved maintenance records, reviews of cockpit protection and better training for emergencies.

The report described the recommendations as "robust" and said they "should minimise the likelihood of a recurrence or similar tragedy".

articles.title: Pakistan braces for showdown as talks collapse, Imran Khan’s party pushes ahead with march
articles.summary: Pakistan’s opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party will proceed with its planned long march towards Islamabad after a second round of talks with
articles.body: Pakistan’s opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party will proceed with its planned long march towards Islamabad after a second round of talks with the government ended without a deal on access to jailed former prime minister Imran Khan.The negotiations began at 4 pm on Saturday and continued into the early hours of Sunday, but the two sides failed to resolve their differences. The main dispute centred on PTI’s demand for an immediate meeting with Khan, including access to his personal doctor.PTI had initially planned to start the long march on September 27 but postponed it to October 4 after the federal government introduced measures aimed at preventing the protest.PTI demands access to Imran KhanThe party wants an immediate meeting with Khan and has demanded that he be taken to a hospital where his personal doctors can examine him.Khan, 73, has been in jail since 2023 after being convicted in a corruption case. He is currently held at the high-security Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi.PTI has also called for the release of Khan’s sisters and other people arrested ahead of the protest. It wants a proper medical examination of Khan’s wife, Bushra Bibi, and has demanded that their legal cases be heard without interference.The government, however, insisted that PTI first cancel the protest before it would consider allowing its leaders to meet Khan, according to sources. PTI rejected that condition and wanted access to its jailed leader before deciding whether to call off the march.Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayin-e-Pakistan leader Senator Allama Nasir Abbas said the negotiations had failed because the two sides could not agree on the roles of the federal and provincial governments in dealing with terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, as well as access to Khan.“No understanding could be reached regarding the respective roles of the province and the federal government concerning terrorism in the province, and the matter of a meeting with Imran Khan remains unresolved,” Abbas, who is also Leader of the Opposition in the Senate, said.“We endeavoured to reach a conclusion, but the deadlock persists -- specifically regarding access to Khan Sahib's personal physician,” he added.Government and PTI blame each otherMinister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry said the talks failed mainly because the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government could not guarantee that it would cooperate with the federal government in the fight against terrorism in the future.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is governed by PTI, and the province is also where the planned march will begin.Pakistan Peoples Party leader Sherry Rehman, who took part in the negotiations, said the government delegation had discussed all the opposition's demands.“Unfortunately, the draft [agreement] was changed four times after it was agreed upon,” she told Geo News, adding that she would not go into the details.Long march to begin from Khyber PakhtunkhwaKhyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi announced at 12:46 am that the protest would go ahead.He said supporters from Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu and Lakki Marwat would join the march at Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat at 1 pm on Sunday.The convoy is scheduled to stop near Karak for the night before leaving at 12:30 pm the following day and staying overnight near Kohat.On October 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram and Orakzai will join the convoy as it moves towards Peshawar, with the group expected to spend the night near Mattani.Afridi said the caravan would leave Budh Bair in Peshawar on the afternoon of October 7. Supporters from other parts of Peshawar will join at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza before the convoy moves towards Charsadda.“The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange,” he said.The protesters are scheduled to leave Charsadda Interchange at 12:30 pm on October 8 after supporters from Charsadda and Mohmand join them.Afridi said people from across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa would gather at Khairabad later that day before the next stage of the march is announced.“God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there,” he said.The federal government has warned that the protesters will not be allowed to enter Islamabad. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s political adviser Rana Sanaullah said authorities would prevent the march from reaching the capital.“No one would be allowed to enter Islamabad,” he told reporters.The government had earlier said it would block roads leading into Islamabad with shipping containers and deploy additional security personnel to prevent the protesters from entering the capital.You use AI every day. articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis say they attacked Aramco facility in Riyadh with missiles, drones
articles.summary: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on ​Saturday they had targeted an Aramco facility ‌in the Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, saying the attack was in ​retaliation for Saudi attacks on Yemen’s ​Sanaa and other provinces.
articles.body: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on ​Saturday they had targeted an Aramco facility ‌in the Saudi capital Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, saying the attack was in ​retaliation for Saudi attacks on Yemen’s ​Sanaa and other provinces. A large plume ⁠of smoke and fire was seen rising ​in the vicinity of an Aramco facility ​in Riyadh earlier on Saturday, a witness told Reuters. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities of an ​attack on an Aramco facility. Aramco did ​not immediately respond to a request for comment. The reported ‌attack ⁠comes amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy ​infrastructure. The Houthis ​said last ⁠week they had attacked Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu with ​missiles and drones. Saudi Arabia said ​at ⁠the time that it had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis towards ⁠Taif ​and the Yanbu area, ​but did not report damage to Aramco facilities.

articles.title: Gaza’s Christians mourn mother and daughter killed in Israeli attack
articles.summary: Maysa Abu Daoud and her daughter Mary al-Najjar among five Palestinians killed in Gaza City attack.
articles.body:
The Latin patriarch of Jerusalem, Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, has expressed his “deep sorrow and grief” over the “tragic” killing of two Christian women in an Israeli air attack on Gaza City.

Maysa Abu Daoud and her daughter Mary al-Najjar were among five Palestinians killed in the attack that hit the ground floor of a building in the Remal neighbourhood on Saturday, in the latest Israeli violation of a United States-brokered “ceasefire” agreement with the Palestinian group Hamas.

In a statement, the patriarch extended his “heartfelt condolences” to the loved ones of the two women and to the Christian community in Gaza.

Their funeral took place on Saturday at Saint Porphyrius Church in Gaza City’s Old City.

The two women were Palestinian Christians from Gaza City who devoted their time to helping parishioners and displaced people sheltering at the Holy Family Church, according to Palestine’s Higher Presidential Committee for Church Affairs.

The committee’s chairman, Ramzi Khoury, described their deaths as a “painful loss” for their families, the church and its parishioners.

Mary’s son, 14-year-old Fouad al-Najjar, told the Anadolu news agency the strike hit the building at about 1:30am (22:30 GMT).

“My grandmother and my mother died. May God have mercy on them,” he said.

Al-Najjar appealed for an end to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, saying Palestinians were losing their loved ones every day.

“We are exhausted by this war and have endured so much,” he said. “For almost three years, we have been living through the same destruction, the same grief and the same war.”

Palestinian Lutheran pastor Munther Isaac, who serves in Ramallah and directs the Bethlehem Institute for Peace and Justice, wrote on X: “The genocide continues in Gaza.”

The Gaza Strip is home to fewer than 1,000 Christians. The community was already small before the war, and many of its members have been killed since then in attacks on their homes and churches throughout the war that began in October 2023.

On October 19, 2023, an attack on the Saint Porphyrius Church compound killed at least 18 people. Two months later, the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem said an Israeli sniper shot dead a woman and her daughter inside the Holy Family parish compound in Gaza.

An Israeli strike on the Holy Family Catholic Church compound on July 17, 2025 also killed three people and wounded others, including parish priest Father Gabriel Romanelli.

According to the Ministry of Health in Gaza, Israeli attacks have killed at least 74,228 people, including at least 1,445 since the start of the “ceasefire” in October 2025.
